display.purpose: The SKÖLL masthead wordmark only, set in amber. Not the score.

score.purpose: The score glyphs, set in the mono data face (700, 24px, tabular-nums) and seated in an amber stamp box in each row's left column.

repo.purpose: owner/repo, the primary line of a bulletin row.

meta.purpose: The source · tag · date meta line and source names.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Floating layers only: settings popover, Run menu, prompt slide-over panel. Never on sheet content.

motion.name: register-snap
motion.purpose: The overprint ghost snapping into register on breakout hover/focus; a print-press step, never an eased float.

notes: The score number is set in the mono data face (var(--mono), 700, 24px, tabular-nums, -0.5px), not the Anton display face. The amber stamp box (fill/tint/outline by tier) carries it, but the glyphs are mono.

Anton ('Skoll Display') is a one-voice display: the SKÖLL masthead wordmark only. The wordmark ships amber (h1 { color: var(--sun) }), line-height 1 with a 5px padding-top. The runic mark beside it is muted mono.
border-radius is 0 system-wide; the only curve is the 8px source dot (50%).
Body carries a 5px radial-dot halftone background-image (the riso paper grain).
prefers-reduced-motion disables the overprint offset entirely (title held in register).
Cool blue (--ink-blue) is live on the focus-tag chips (text at rest, full fill on the active filter).
Telegram integration lives in the Settings popover; the weekly page reuses the bulletin rows, mono tables, and a clickable Best/Okay/Passed tier filter.

Divergence from the direction contract: ::selection, caret-color and accent-color ship as amber (--sun), not the ink-on-paper plate the contract named. The build wins; recorded as-is. The inverted Ink plate is used for pressed toggles (source tabs, language).

narrative.overview: The daily scan printed as a dated security broadsheet — one dense, single-column sheet of what rose today, read top-down by score. It is a riso press artifact (the 2600 / Phrack / DEF CON overprint lineage): a warm near-black paper ground under a fine halftone tint, two inks only, and a visible modular grid left honest as armature rather than hidden behind cards. Mode is Operate: density, scanability and keyboard use outrank expression. The page refuses the auto-fill grid of equal cards and the characterless system-font flatness that made the prior dashboard read as a template; in their place is one aligned column at real tabular density, every datum in monospace, and a condensed poster face carrying the one voice that matters — the SKÖLL masthead wordmark — while the score joins the monospace data spine, stamped into an amber box. Dark is the default; light is a cool newsprint, never cream. The brand lives in precise press details — the amber wordmark and runic mark, the amber score stamp, the fore-edge extent rail, and the overprint-register ghost on breakout rows.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black riso ground (#16130f) under a 5px halftone dot tint.
Exactly two inks: sun amber and cool blue, over paper-ink text.
Square everything (0 radius); 1px hairline rules form a visible column grid.
One dense bulletin column, never a card grid; a fore-edge rail shows extent.
Poster display (Anton) for the SKÖLL wordmark only; every datum, the score included, is monospace with tabular figures.
Signature: OVERPRINT REGISTER — the breakout row's amber ghost snaps home.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: The world runs on exactly two chromatic inks — sun amber and cool blue — over paper, ground and border neutrals. Amber is the signal (score stamp top tier, wordmark, Run, breakout, rail, masthead rule, focus); blue is the focus-tag chip. Alarm red is an exception reserved for a suspicious finding. A third decorative hue is a hierarchy problem, not a color problem.

rules.name: The Inverted-Plate Rule
rules.body: A selected or pressed UI toggle — a source tab, a language button — reverses to an Ink plate with Ground text, not amber. Amber is signal; the plate reversal is UI state. (Browser text selection, caret and accent-color are amber in the shipped build, diverging from the contract's named ink-plate selection; the build wins and is recorded as-is.)

rules.name: The Mono-Datum Rule
rules.body: Anything a pentester would copy, compare or sort — repo name, score, date, stars, stars/day, matched keywords, source name — is monospace with tabular figures. The score is a datum, not a poster element. Prose (descriptions) is the only system-sans text on a row.

rules.name: The One-Voice Display Rule
rules.body: The Anton display face is spent on exactly one thing: the SKÖLL masthead wordmark. It never sets the score, a section header, a button, or a label. The score belongs to the mono data spine inside its amber box; the stamp box earns the loudness, not the letterforms. Uppercase belongs to the poster wordmark, not to UI labels.

rules.name: The Flat-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Anything that is part of the sheet is flat — depth is tone + hairline. A drop shadow is a claim that an element floats above the page; only menus and the slide-over may make that claim.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Amber fill on a control means 'run the scan.' No other button is filled amber; secondary controls are surface + hairline.

dos: Do keep amber to signal — score stamp (top), wordmark, Run, breakout, rail, masthead rule, focus rings (The Two Inks Rule).
Do set every datum (repo, score, date, stars, counts, keywords) in monospace with tabular figures; the score is a datum in an amber box.
Do keep corners square (0 radius); the only circle is the 8px source dot.
Do convey depth with tone + 1px hairlines; reserve the Overlay shadow for floating menus and the slide-over.
Do leave the column grid visible as an honest armature (interior hairlines).
Do default to dark; render light as cool newsprint.
donts: Don't use the Anton display face for anything but the SKÖLL wordmark — not the score, not headers, not labels.
Don't fill a second control amber, or introduce a third decorative hue.
Don't put a shadow on a bulletin row, stamp, chip or the rail.
Don't fall back to an auto-fill grid of equal cards; the sheet is one dense aligned column.
Don't use a cream background or terracotta accent in either theme.
Don't use ALL-CAPS UI labels, 'WORD —' headings, or glyph/emoji icons.
Don't let any row cause horizontal page scroll at 375px.
